video_title: LeBron & Steve Nash Reveal the Secrets to Elite Shooting

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James on his preference for shooting against the laces
quotes.excerpt: I'm a guy who don't like shooting against the laces.
quotes.quote: I'm a guy who don't like shooting against the laces. Sometimes I'll come up, a quick stop, and I'm about to raise, and I can feel the laces not fixed. I'll turn that into a pump fake.
quotes.social_post: LeBron James reveals he is so particular about shooting mechanics that he avoids shooting against the laces and even adjusts the ball for teammates based on their preference.

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Nash on why NBA players struggle with free throws
quotes.excerpt: As a good free throw shooter, it's hard for the common fans to understand how good NBA players struggle.
quotes.quote: As a good free throw shooter, it's hard for the common fans to understand how good NBA players struggle with free throws. Can you help me understand?
quotes.social_post: Steve Nash discusses the difficulty of understanding why elite NBA players sometimes struggle with free throws.

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Nash on how Stephen Curry changed the game
quotes.excerpt: Stephen Curry changed the game in that he shoots almost the way I shot as a kid.
quotes.quote: Stephen Curry changed the game in that he shoots almost the way I shot as a kid. It's straight through. It doesn't stop in the pocket, and so he has lots of legs. But I mean, that's still crazy to make.
quotes.social_post: Steve Nash breaks down the mechanics of Stephen Curry, noting that his shot is straight through and does not stop in the pocket, which allows him to generate incredible power.

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Nash on the importance of footwork for shooting
quotes.excerpt: Footwork, first and foremost, because it gets you on balance and allows you to get lift.
quotes.quote: Footwork, first and foremost, because it gets you on balance and allows you to get lift. Lift, you got to create force, you got to create power to get the ball up in the air to allow the hand to be soft. Rhythm, that force then creates rhythm. One thing that I think is important is your release point. Some guys have been good at this, I think Jaylen Brown actually sometimes hangs or shoots almost on the way down on his middies. But I think the rule of thumb is you want to shoot as or before you get to the top, because then you're using your legs and you have the same, and it's repeatable.
quotes.social_post: Steve Nash explains the importance of footwork and release points, noting that Jaylen Brown sometimes shoots on the way down, but the ideal is to release before the top of the jump.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James on learning to shoot by watching Michael Jordan
quotes.excerpt: My shooting journey is literally like watching Michael Jordan.
quotes.quote: My shooting journey is literally like watching Michael Jordan. But the thing I didn't realize is how balanced Michael Jordan was. I saw a fadeaway. So the flick of the wrist, the head back, I saw a fadeaway. So when I started to see that I had some athletic genes, I maybe picked up some bad habits in my shooting because I can emulate that. So I was shooting fadeaways as like a freshman in high school, and I was making them, but I didn't realize that I was picking up bad habits along that time because I didn't study the fact that, okay, yeah, MJ is doing that, but you're not even seeing how on balance he is.
quotes.social_post: LeBron James admits he picked up bad shooting habits in high school by trying to emulate Michael Jordan fadeaways without understanding the balance behind them.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James on learning shooting details from Chris Jent
quotes.excerpt: The detail started, shout out Chris Jent. Elite shooter, played at Ohio State back in the day.
quotes.quote: The detail started, shout out Chris Jent. Elite shooter, played at Ohio State back in the day. He joined Mike Brown when Mike Brown took over in Cleveland early in my years, and I used to watch him shoot in practice. He used to shoot like on the side, or he would be, you know, when the coaches kind of be the scout team sometimes, he would shoot the ball. And even though he's a lefty, it was the same beautiful shot Chris Jent every time, rubbing that, rubbing them ribs, follow through, getting that, getting that arc on it. And I just started to work with him a lot. And it went from during the season to transferring to the off season. So I give a lot of credit to where my shot is today from where it was to Chris Jent.
quotes.social_post: LeBron James credits former teammate and coach Chris Jent for helping him refine his shooting mechanics during his early years in Cleveland.

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Nash on the necessity of repetition for shooting
quotes.excerpt: For it to be a habit, for it to be repeatable, for it to be stress test, you have to put in those like ugly hours.
quotes.quote: For it to be a habit, for it to be repeatable, for it to be stress test, you have to put in those like ugly hours of just doing it. Right, and so your body now cannot do the other, which takes time. He got me comfortable with being uncomfortable. That was like one of my first stages of like falling in love with being uncomfortable.
quotes.social_post: Steve Nash on the grind of shooting: You have to put in the ugly hours to make mechanics repeatable and get comfortable with being uncomfortable.

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Nash on the importance of feeling in shooting
quotes.excerpt: It's not necessarily visualize, it's feeling. It's feeling the rhythm, the technique, the body position.
quotes.quote: It's not necessarily visualize, it's feeling. It's feeling the rhythm, the technique, the body position. I think doing a mental rehearsal or visualization with the feelings is impactful.
quotes.social_post: Steve Nash emphasizes that shooting is more about feeling the rhythm and body position than just visualization.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James on fixing his shot mechanics
quotes.excerpt: When the ball is coming towards me, I'm almost fixing it. Well, not almost, I am fixing the laces before I even get to my shot.
quotes.quote: When the ball is coming towards me, I'm almost fixing it. Well, not almost, I am fixing the laces before I even get to my shot, you know, or even off the dribble, I'm trying to fix the laces. And I didn't realize that a lot of players are like that as well. So like any team I go to or play with or guys, like if I'm new to the team, I always ask them like, how do you, how do you like to shoot the ball? And they be like, I like, you like, what do you mean? I like, do you like laces or no laces? Do you prefer? Because when I deliver the ball, I want to be able to deliver the ball right to you, so all you have to do is, and it's not going to be like perfect every time, but sometimes you got to like balance it, you got to spin it, but like I want to know how you shoot the ball. So when I deliver it to you, either if you, if you like the laces, the ball is coming to you like this, so it's already in the pocket, or if you don't, then I know to put a little spin on it too.
quotes.social_post: LeBron James explains how he tries to deliver passes based on his teammates shooting preferences, adjusting the spin so the ball is ready to shoot immediately.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James on players who are born shooters
quotes.excerpt: I forgot J.R. Smith, Mike Miller, James Jones, Kyle Korver. Like those are four names that I played with personally.
quotes.quote: I forgot J.R. Smith, Mike Miller, James Jones, Kyle Korver. Like those are four names that I played with personally that are, Mike Miller had an unbelievable look of shot. J.R. Smith super powerful, strong, compact shot. James Jones super compact, shoot it all the way to the top of the arena. Kyle Korver was like a, like a lasers, it gets off so fast, you know. And guys that shot every day, you know, like, clearly, but like, needed it. It was literally their breathing. They had to.
quotes.social_post: LeBron James reflects on the elite shooters he has played with, highlighting the unique styles of JR Smith, Mike Miller, James Jones, and Kyle Korver.
